## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes: switching conversations can leave chat on old messages or freeze the chat window, which also causes recurring failures in otherwise unrelated CI runs.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

Switching conversations should land on the newest messages without freezing, while still not interrupting someone who is reading.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The freeze is a WinUI bug, not our timing. `ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView` runs a synchronous layout; if that layout recycles the target row, `ItemsView::GetElementIndex` keeps asking for the same container and never exits. Upstream fixed this in [microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml#12320](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/pull/12320) (commit `54d01b8`), but no supported Windows App SDK release contains it: the supported 2.6.5 ships identical code to our 2.6.4, so a package bump does not help.

Chat tail navigation therefore no longer calls that API. It realizes the newest row through the timeline's `ItemsRepeater` outside layout, waits for native layout to settle, reacquires the live container once with full revalidation, and calls `StartBringIntoView` on that container. Preparation gets one bounded recovery. If preparation or reacquisition still fails during the initial landing, the existing bounded landing check retries the newest row instead of leaving the conversation at the top. A landing is confirmed only when the native list is showing the current rows, because an empty or stale list also reads as "at the bottom". User input, conversation replacement, unload and disposal cancel pending work. The earlier far-edge anchoring and in-flight deferral remain, along with the reviewed input-cancellation correction. The architecture ledger records the workaround and when to retire it (once a supported WinUI release contains the upstream fix).

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. Include before/after evidence for visual
changes when it clarifies the result.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

The previous head (`de254d84`) froze locally in `RepeatedSessionSwitchingKeepsNativeTimelineResponsive`. A private dump showed the UI thread inside `ItemsView::StartBringItemIntoViewInternal -> ItemsView::GetElementIndex`, requesting index 239. Disassembly of the shipped `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.dll` located the non-progressing loop, and the shipped bytes match the code that upstream fixed.

The current head adds three mounted native regressions. The transient-source recovery test fails with recovery disabled and passes with it restored. The held-missing-source test (`TailNavigation_InitialLandingRetriesWhenSourceStaysMissingThroughPreparation`) timed out with the view stranded at the top (offset 0 of 25208) when the failure path was temporarily reverted to the old give-up behavior, and passes with the retry. It now holds the source missing for 15 and for 45 frames (Reactor reasserts the source on a later render, so the hold uses a property callback). With confirmation temporarily switched back to the plain near-bottom check, the 45-frame case failed: the log showed `Landed near=True off=0 ext=0 src=null` and the view stayed at offset 0. With the current-rows check both cases pass. The recycled-target test drives recycling through `RecommendedAnchorIndex`. Before the fix, that scenario would hang rather than fail, so that test proves the post-fix behavior, not a red-before result.

<details>
<summary>Historical hosted stress evidence for earlier heads (not proof of this head)</summary>

| Run | Source | Voice passed / total | Session-switch passed / total | Full fixture suites passed / total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [42550670148](https://github.com/shanselman/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/42550670148) | main plus diagnostics | 67 / 72 | Not looped | Not run |
| [42554838495](https://github.com/shanselman/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/42554838495) | earlier anchoring revision | 120 / 120 | 51 / 60 | 8 / 8 |
| [42558001798](https://github.com/shanselman/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/42558001798) | diagnostic commit `2a4e4778`, before the cancellation correction | 120 / 120 | 150 / 150 | 8 / 8 |

These passing runs did not prevent the later local freeze, which is why the native root cause was pursued instead of more retries.
</details>

## Validation

<!--
Include exact commands and pass/fail counts. Baseline after code changes:
- `./build.ps1`
- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore`

For inventory-bound proof, link the local execution summary described in

Completed for this head (`52a420d2`) before commit, using the same file contents:

- Tray focused tests (`ReactorTimeline_`, `InitialTailConfirmation_`, `TailNavigation`, `Architecture` filters): 54 passed.
- Mounted `TailNavigation_` tests (Debug), run 3 times: 4 passed each time (both hold lengths). The 45-frame hold failed with the old near-bottom confirmation and passed after restoring the fix.
- `.\scripts\validate-docs.ps1` and `git diff --check`: passed.

Completed for the previous head (`7e1fa8ec`): architecture ledger tests 6 passed, chat owner source contracts 73 passed, mounted `ReactorChatLayoutProofTests` 10 passed, and Shared tests 4876 passed with 24 skipped and 0 failed.
- `.\scripts\validate-docs.ps1` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `.\build.ps1`, the non-Dev Release WinUI build (`.\build.ps1 -Project WinUI -Configuration Release` with process-scoped `$env:RequireSignedCleanupHost='false'`, which is unsigned local build evidence), and the Debug and Release UI test builds: passed.

**Current-head acceptance outcome (`52a420d2`): partial, not clean.**

- `./build.ps1`, `./build.ps1 -Project WinUI -Configuration Release` (with process-scoped `$env:RequireSignedCleanupHost='false'`), and Debug/Release UI test builds: passed.
- `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore`: 4,876 passed, 24 skipped, 0 failed. `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore`: 5,309 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed.
- `./scripts/validate-docs.ps1` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Debug Gateway fixture suite: 81/81 passed. Release Gateway fixture suite: 81/81 passed.
- Repeated proof: all 30 Debug and all 30 Release runs passed both `RepeatedSessionSwitchingKeepsNativeTimelineResponsive` and `HistoricalFractionalVoiceConversationRendersWithoutLoadingPlaceholder` (60 passes of each test across both configurations).
- Mounted chat suite: Debug aborted twice in `PlacementPickers_SearchSelectAndPrepareOnlyOnSend(width: 320)` with a test-host `InvalidCastException` during XAML `MeasureOverride` and `Element is already the child of another element`; each aborted run recorded 3 earlier tests passing. The same 12 placement tests passed in 15 isolated runs (180/180). Release completed with 139 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed; the required mounted suite did not satisfy the no-skips gate.
- This intermittent mounted-suite abort is not explained by the chat-tail change, but it means full acceptance is not green. The run was not retried to claim a green result. Hosted CI on this PR head is green; this local acceptance gap remains.

## Real Behavior Proof

<!--
Paste at least one current-head proof item that directly demonstrates the
changed behavior. Use copied live output, screenshots or video, UI diagnostics,

logs, or linked artifacts.
-->

- Environment tested: local Windows x64, unpackaged app, synthetic loopback Gateway fixture, disposable profiles and local MCP ports. No shared Gateway or normal user profile.
- PR head or commit tested: `52a420d2`; hosted CI is green. Local synthetic-fixture tests executed 60/60 switching repetitions and 60/60 fractional-voice repetitions across Debug and Release. The mounted Debug suite aborted twice in the unrelated placement-picker test; Release mounted suite had 2 skipped tests.
- Exact steps: full acceptance launcher `launch-tail-acceptance.ps1 -Artifacts files\direct-tail-final-v4` stopped at the Debug mounted-suite host crash. A subsequent gap-fill run covered the fixture and repeated suites in both configurations; its full mounted results are recorded in Validation above.
- Evidence after fix: held-missing-source native regression passed 3 consecutive runs at both 15- and 45-frame holds; both repeated behavior proofs passed 60/60 across Debug and Release.
- Observed result: switching and voice behavior remained responsive in all repeated runs. Full mounted-suite acceptance is incomplete because of the intermittent unrelated test-host crash and Release skips.
- Screenshot or artifact links verified? (`Yes`/`No`/`N/A`): No. The native dump is private and will not be uploaded.
- Not verified or blocked: clean completion of the full mounted chat UI suite on this head; signed release builds. Independent re-review found no P0-P3 issues. The native dump is private and will not be uploaded. These are synthetic fixture runs, not provider, real Gateway or installer proof.
